newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gaddum says German repo rules have desired effect.
newsitem.headline: Gaddum says German repo rules have desired effect.

text.p: Bundesbank deputy president Johann Gaddum said on Tuesday he believed the central bank's decision to free some security repurchase agreements, or repos, from minimum reserve requirements has had the desired effect.
"Our goal is to build up the repo business in Germany," Gaddum told a news conference called to announce the issuance of a new strippable 30-year bond.
Repo business in Germany has been free from minimum reserve requirements since January 1997, according to the Bundesbank.
The German repo market in the past has been viewed as being relatively undeveloped since German banks had been subjected to the Bundesbank's minimum reserve requirement.
Most major banks have moved their mark repo business to Germany from London since the decision was taken.
